title: OneDrive and SharePoint: respond to access requests in the Share dialog
summary: The briefing passes: the planned behaviour matches the roadmap, and Microsoft documentation supports the sharing controls, audit searches and product-level licensing. Minor corrections should acknowledge differing Microsoft navigation wording and raise the action rating because January's target is now within 60 days.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether this experience arrives on by default or behind a setting.
claims.quote: Searched: OneDrive SharePoint roadmap 578856 respond access requests Share dialog default setting license; OneDrive SharePoint Share dialog access requests tenant disable enable PowerShell default guest. Read roadmap and Limit sharing; no feature default stated.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this specific Share-dialog access-request feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "578856"; "OneDrive" "Respond to access requests"; "Share dialog" "pending requests" "OneDrive". Read returned excerpts and Limit sharing; results describe existing sharing or file uploads, not this roadmap feature.

claims.claim: Only site admins and members of the site's Owners group can process requests in its Access Requests list today.
claims.quote: These issues occur because the affected users are not site admins (previously called site collection administrators) or members of the Owners group for the site. Only users with these specific permissions can process requests to the Access Requests list.

claims.claim: The Owners group must have Full Control permissions to the Access Requests list.
claims.quote: For users who are members of the Owners group for the site, an another requirement is that the Owners group must have Full Control permissions to access the Access Requests list.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Owners-only file, folder and site sharing is configured inside a site through gear icon > Site permissions > Sharing settings > Change how members can share > Only site owners can share files, folders, and the site.
claims.quote: In the site, select the gear icon, and then select Site permissions. Under Sharing settings, select Change how members can share. Select Only site owners can share files, folders, and the site.
claims.fix: Keep the documented site path. Add to Governance controls: 'Limit sharing documents this route inside the site; the sensitivity-label guidance instead describes the equivalent option under SharePoint admin center > Site permissions > Site Sharing > Change how members can share > Sharing permissions.' Both pages are already cited.

claims.claim: Set-Label -Identity <label> -AdvancedSettings @{MembersCanShare="MemberShareNone"} configures a sensitivity label for the owners-only sharing option.

claims.claim: The label's configured settings take effect when it is applied to a supported container.
claims.quote: When you apply a sensitivity label to a supported container, the label automatically applies the sensitivity category and configured protection settings to the workspace.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The site's access-request control is at gear icon > Site permissions > Sharing settings > Change how members can share > Allow access requests.
claims.quote: In the site, select the gear icon, and then select Site permissions. Under Sharing settings, select Change how members can share. Turn off Allow access requests, and then select Save.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented an automation operation that sets whether people without access can request access to a site.
claims.quote: Searched: SharePoint Online Allow access requests disable enable PowerShell RequestAccessEmail; "Allow access requests" "API" SharePoint; "RequestAccessEmail" "empty". Opened Web.RequestAccessEmail: writable string, but no documented enable/disable semantics.

claims.claim: Microsoft's troubleshooting guidance requires a site collection administrator to enable access requests.
claims.quote: To resolve the errors, enable access requests for the affected site collection. You must be a site collection administrator to enable this feature.

claims.claim: Audit searches are available in the Microsoft Purview portal under Audit > Search.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal. Select the Audit solution card. If the Audit solution card isn't displayed, select View all solutions and then select Audit from the Core section. On the Search page, configure the following search criteria as applicable:

claims.claim: Search-UnifiedAuditLog -StartDate <ExDateTime> -EndDate <ExDateTime> -Operations AccessRequestCreated,AccessRequestAccepted,AccessRequestDenied searches these access-request operations.
claims.quote:
Search-UnifiedAuditLog
    -EndDate <ExDateTime>
    -StartDate <ExDateTime>
    [-Operations <String[]>]
The Operations parameter filters the log entries by operation. You can enter multiple values separated by commas.

claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Microsoft Purview portal to search the audit log. To access audit cmdlets, you must be assigned the Audit Logs or View-Only Audit Logs roles in the Exchange admin center.

claims.claim: With owners-only sharing configured, direct-access and Specific people link sharing by site members goes to the site owner for approval.

claims.quote: Searched: "Share dialog" "access requests" default guests bulk licensing tenant setting; OneDrive SharePoint Share dialog access requests tenant disable enable PowerShell default guest. Read roadmap, Limit sharing and search excerpts; none describes guest requests in this dialog.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not described how the new dialog presents approvals routed to owners under owners-only sharing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Share dialog" "pending requests" "OneDrive"; "OneDrive" "Respond to access requests". Read roadmap and Limit sharing; the former describes pending requests generally and the latter existing owner approval, without explaining their new presentation.

claims.claim: The table's site-sharing UI paths configure settings inside each site.

claims.claim: The existing access-request process sends requests to a configured email address.
claims.quote: Requests for access are sent to the email address that's specified in step 5.

claims.claim: No source states that this feature changes existing site access-request settings.
claims.quote: Searched: OneDrive SharePoint Share dialog access requests tenant disable enable PowerShell default guest; "OneDrive" "Respond to access requests". Read roadmap, Limit sharing and request-access troubleshooting; none states this feature resets existing settings.

claims.claim: The prepare action rating fits a medium-risk redesign targeted for January CY2027 on the November 27, 2026 run.
claims.quote: action: "prepare"; risk: "medium"; targetDate: "January CY2027". The briefing says requests will appear in a new place and advises reviewing sharing settings before rollout; January 1 is 35 days after the run date.
claims.fix: Change front matter action from "prepare" to "act-now": the standard counts the month-only January CY2027 target from January 1, within 60 days of November 27, and the medium-risk redesign requires a sharing decision and communication before it lands.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes access grants as decisions made by people in the dialog.
claims.quote: From there, they can choose the level of access to grant, approve or decline requests individually or in bulk, and message the requester before deciding.
